This is absence-of-evidence across secondary sources, not a direct official 'no CCA' statement — needs verification via CPUC's CCA service-area map or a City of Fresno utilities communication before recording a value.

value.description: New applications and waitlist applications for ratepayer-funded SGIP budgets closed on December 30, 2025. New AB 209 applications have a June 30, 2028 deadline. The 2026 SGIP rate table publishes $3.10/W for solar and $1.10/Wh for storage in applicable Residential Solar and Storage Equity categories. Household eligibility and live budget availability vary by category and program administrator; check the official Program Metrics tracker before relying on an incentive.
value.eligibility: Eligibility varies by 2026 SGIP budget category, program administrator, property, income/pathway, project rules, and live funding availability.

battery_programs.notes: SGIP program data refreshed on 2026-08-26 from the official 2026 Handbook and live Program Metrics. Earlier locality records contained 2025 opening/availability language. This record does not assert household eligibility, reservation availability, or a guaranteed incentive; current category and program-administrator status must be checked before reliance.

SolarAPP+ approval confirmation
value.required_when: SolarAPP+-eligible residential rooftop systems (single-family and duplex only)

required_documents.notes: Per Fresno Municipal Code Section 11-111(b)(2): an Eligibility Checklist for Expedited Solar Photovoltaic Permitting shall be completed to determine if the project qualifies. The SolarAPP+ confirmation-upload step is independently confirmed via the City's own SolarAPP+ page (S1).

value: For a Small Residential Rooftop Solar Energy System eligible for expedited review, only one inspection shall be required, which may include a consolidated inspection
If a system fails the inspection, a subsequent inspection is authorized

value.notes: Multiple independent sources consistently describe SolarAPP+-eligible residential (single-family/duplex) solar permits in Fresno as issued 'in real time' once the contractor uploads the SolarAPP+ confirmation to the city's Accela system — i.e. same-day/immediate issuance. No source found states a timeline for the standard (non-SolarAPP+, e.g. commercial) permit path.

other_conditions: Contractor must be licensed and registered as a SolarAPP+ installer
Confirmation must be uploaded to the City's Accela Citizens Access (ACA) electronic permitting system
Commercial solar installations do not qualify for SolarAPP+ and must use the standard permit process
